subject: Follow-up: FinPay demo + TCO compare
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 27, 2026 at 5:05 PM PST
Subject: FinPay demo + next steps / TCO info

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery + demo and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- High-throughput token-level scoring for transaction summarization and fraud signal enrichment (~200–500 requests/sec peak; batch-friendly).
- Tight p95 latency target for inference tail (~<250ms for single-request workflow; higher acceptable for batch jobs).
- Strong cost controls — want to understand unit economics (per-1M tokens), and impact of batching + prefix cache.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + VPC/private option for higher assurance (Jake, I know you’re looping in secops).

What I captured as next tests we should run:
1) Cost/TCO baseline: provide a per-1M tokens cost estimate across Redwood hosted, Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool), and two comparison points (AWS Bedrock and OpenAI) with clear assumptions on tokenization, avg tokens/req, caching and batching.
2) Performance test: a 1-hour simulated workload using your sample prompts (can use the sheet you mentioned) to measure p50/p95 latency, throughput, and GPU utilization.
3) Cache/batch sensitivity: a small set of runs varying batch sizes (1/8/16) and simulated cache hit rates (0/20/50%) to show cost delta.

Ask from you to kick off tests:
- Share an anonymized sample of typical prompts and traffic distribution (you mentioned an export file — thanks).
- Confirm whether we should include embeddings workload in the first pass or focus on generation only.

Attached is a quick Redwood pricing snapshot to orient the conversation (redwood_pricing_snapshot.pdf). I’ll follow up with a short TCO breakdown and assumptions by early next week.

Proposed next meeting: 30 min on Mon/Tue to review TCO and agree on the test run. Marcus — I’ll hand off the benchmarking plan to you once Sarah confirms the sample.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap and the snapshot. This is exactly the direction we need. A few quick clarifying items before you put together the TCO sheet:  

1) Throughput: our peak request mix is roughly 350 req/s for Summarize (avg 220 tokens in, 80 tokens out). We also have off-peak batch jobs that can be run asynchronously.
2) Cache behavior: a decent portion of requests share prefixes (transaction headers). Realistic prefix cache hit rate from our logs is around ~30% but there’s variability across merchants.
3) Context length: we want to allow up to 2k tokens for longer cases, but average session is < 1k.
4) Embeddings: we will have a smaller embedding pipeline (~50 req/s) for search indexing — please include a per-1M vectors/embedding cost if you can, but focus the first pass on generation TCO.

I attached the sample workload and token distribution (finpay_tco.xlsx). Can you include a comparison versus AWS Bedrock (for the same open models) and OpenAI (gpt-4 style as a proxy)? If you can provide both hosted-per-request numbers and an indicative Dedicated/Committed monthly number, that will help our finance team.

Also please call out assumptions: tokenization (tiktoken-like), batching sizes, and effect of 20/50% cache hits on effective cost per 1M tokens.

We’re looping in Jake for security/compliance — he may ask for SOC2 artifacts and private deployment details.

Thanks — happy to meet Mon 10am PT to review if that works.

—Sarah
Sarah Collins

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, Mar 1, 2026 at 3:42 PM PST
Subject: Re: FinPay demo + next steps / TCO info

Thanks Sarah — got the sample (appreciate the export). Below is a first-pass TCO and testing plan with explicit assumptions. This is meant to give your finance and infra teams something to evaluate; we can make the numbers more precise once we run the benchmark against your sample.

High-level assumptions (applies unless noted):
- Tokenization: tiktoken-like; average request = 220 input tokens + 80 output tokens = 300 tokens total per request.
- 1M tokens = baseline billing unit; we present per-1M tokens for comparability.
- Latency targets: single-request p95 < 250ms (hosted), dedicated tuned for p95 < 200ms at scale.
- Batching effect: batching size 16 assumed for throughput pricing runs; batching reduces per-token GPU overhead but increases latency.
- Cache: prefix cache reduces downstream decoding cost proportional to cache-hit% on KV cache; we model 0%, 30%, 50%.

Per-1M tokens (generation) — indicative costs:
- Redwood Hosted (open model family, production profile): $22 / 1M tokens (no cache) -> effective $15 / 1M at 30% cache -> $11 / 1M at 50% cache.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, mid-utilization): $7 / 1M tokens (with steady utilization and batching) — note this is sensitive to commit level and utilization.
- AWS Bedrock (proxy cost for managed open model endpoints, conservative estimate): $40 / 1M tokens (no cache) -> effective $28 / 1M at 30% cache.
- OpenAI (gpt-like proxy): $55 / 1M tokens (generally higher for closed commercial models; includes model and platform margin).

Embedding cost (per-1M vectors):
- Redwood Hosted embeddings: $6 / 1M vectors (independent pipeline pricing)
- Dedicated embedding pipeline: $2.50 / 1M vectors (when batched and reserved capacity used)

Notes on assumptions and sensitivities:
- Batching: moving from batch=1 to batch=16 reduces per-token GPU overhead ~20–40% depending on model kernel efficiency and sequence length distribution. We’ll show concrete deltas in the benchmark.
- Cache: realistic prefix cache hit of 30% materially reduces billed token count for generation, since repeated prefix KV can be reused for many requests. We model cache savings as direct reductions in generated token work but will measure empirically.
- Committed Dedicated pricing assumes steady utilization (>60%); lower utilization increases effective $/1M.

Recommended tests (what Redwood will run once you confirm sample):
1) Baseline 1-hour run (generation only): replay your finpay_tco.xlsx traffic at production QPS shape to measure p50/p95 latency and throughput, and record raw token counts.
2) Cache sensitivity: run three passes with simulated cache hit rates (0%, ~30%, ~50%) to capture effective billed tokens and latency tradeoffs.
3) Batch sensitivity: test batch sizes 1/8/16 and show throughput vs latency vs cost.
4) Dedicated estimate: if you want a Dedicated POC, we can run an allocated-capacity test for 24–72 hours to capture utilization and present an actual committed pricing quote.

Next steps:
- If you confirm the sample is final, Marcus will schedule the baseline run and share a short benchmark plan (metrics + Grafana links).
- Proposed meeting: Mon 10am PT to review these assumptions and pick the initial test parameters.

I attached a quick spreadsheet mapping the above to monthlyized run examples (we’ll refine after the benchmark): redwood_pricing_snapshot.pdf (same doc I sent earlier).

If helpful I can also provide a short deck that compares latency/throughput curves vs the two hyperscaler comparators.

Thanks — ping me the meeting invite and we’ll get Marcus to start the runs.

Best,
